objects.description: Enumeration of library warning/error severity levels used with the error callback. Higher values indicate more severe conditions, with JBIG2_SEVERITY_FATAL indicating non-recoverable errors.
Bitmask-like options enum for configuring the decoder context. JBIG2_OPTIONS_EMBEDDED indicates the stream is embedded and may use a global context.

Customizable memory allocator interface used by the decoder. Clients can provide alloc, free, and realloc callbacks to control memory usage. If NULL is passed to jbig2_ctx_new, a default malloc-based allocator is used.
Opaque decoder context for processing JBIG2 streams. Construct with jbig2_ctx_new_imp (via jbig2_ctx_new macro) and free with jbig2_ctx_free. Internals are not exposed in this header.
Opaque global context used to share global segments across embedded JBIG2 streams. Create with jbig2_make_global_ctx and free with jbig2_global_ctx_free.

General 1 bpp image structure used by jbig2dec. Pixels are packed in bytes; stride is the byte offset between rows. width and height are in pixels. data points to pixel data; refcount tracks shared ownership. Returned by jbig2_page_out and should be released with jbig2_release_page when no longer needed.

objects.definition: typedef void (*Jbig2ErrorCallback)(void *data, const char *msg, Jbig2Severity severity, uint32_t seg_idx);
objects.description: Function pointer type for user-provided error logging. Receives user data, a message string, severity level, and the segment index (or JBIG2_UNKNOWN_SEGMENT_NUMBER when unknown).

functions.name: jbig2_ctx_new_imp
functions.signature: Jbig2Ctx *jbig2_ctx_new_imp(Jbig2Allocator *allocator, Jbig2Options options, Jbig2GlobalCtx *global_ctx, Jbig2ErrorCallback error_callback, void *error_callback_data, int jbig2_version_major, int jbig2_version_minor);
functions.description: Create a new JBIG2 decoder context. Callers may provide custom memory allocation callbacks (allocator) and an error callback; if allocator is NULL a default malloc-based allocator is used, and if error_callback is NULL a default handler prints fatal errors to stderr. The options parameter configures decoder behavior (e.g., embedded mode). If decoding embedded streams, a Jbig2GlobalCtx created via jbig2_make_global_ctx can be supplied; otherwise pass NULL. The jbig2_version_major/minor parameters are meant to be filled by the wrapper macro jbig2_ctx_new and should match the library’s JBIG2_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR.
requirements: allocator may be NULL to use the default allocator; otherwise it must point to a valid Jbig2Allocator with alloc/free/realloc callbacks.
error_callback may be NULL to use the default handler; otherwise it must be a valid function conforming to Jbig2ErrorCallback and may receive severity and segment index information.
error_callback_data is an opaque pointer passed to error_callback and may be NULL.
If using embedded streams, global_ctx should be a valid Jbig2GlobalCtx (typically from jbig2_make_global_ctx); otherwise pass NULL.
Callers should not manually specify jbig2_version_major/minor; use the jbig2_ctx_new macro which supplies JBIG2_VERSION_MAJOR/JBIG2_VERSION_MINOR.
The returned Jbig2Ctx* must later be released with jbig2_ctx_free.

functions.name: jbig2_ctx_free
functions.description: Free a JBIG2 decoder context previously created with jbig2_ctx_new_imp (or via the jbig2_ctx_new macro). Returns the allocator associated with the context.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Jbig2Ctx returned by jbig2_ctx_new_imp/jbig2_ctx_new and not already freed.
After this call, ctx must not be used again.
The returned Jbig2Allocator* (if any) remains owned by the caller; NULL may be returned if unknown (library-dependent).

functions.name: jbig2_make_global_ctx
functions.description: Create a global context from an existing decoder context, intended for use with embedded JBIG2 streams that share global segments.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, initialized Jbig2Ctx.
The returned Jbig2GlobalCtx* should later be freed with jbig2_global_ctx_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: jbig2_global_ctx_free
functions.description: Free a previously created global context and return its associated allocator.
requirements: global_ctx must be a valid Jbig2GlobalCtx obtained from jbig2_make_global_ctx and not already freed.
After this call, global_ctx must not be used again.

functions.name: jbig2_data_in
functions.signature: int jbig2_data_in(Jbig2Ctx *ctx, const unsigned char *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Submit raw JBIG2 data bytes to the decoder. The decoder consumes up to ‘size’ bytes from ‘data’.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Jbig2Ctx.
data must point to at least ‘size’ bytes of readable memory (size may be zero).
Caller should check the returned int for status; exact return codes/semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: jbig2_page_out
functions.description: Retrieve the next available decoded page image. Returns NULL if no page is currently available. Images are 1 bpp, packed, with fields width, height, stride, and data.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Jbig2Ctx.
If a non-NULL Jbig2Image* is returned, the caller must later call jbig2_release_page(ctx, image) when the image is no longer needed.
The returned image data should be treated as read-only and owned by the decoder until released.

functions.name: jbig2_release_page
functions.description: Mark a page image previously returned by jbig2_page_out as no longer needed, allowing the decoder to reclaim resources.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Jbig2Ctx.
image must be a Jbig2Image previously returned by jbig2_page_out for the same ctx and not already released.

functions.name: jbig2_complete_page
functions.description: Mark the current page as complete, simulating an end-of-page segment. Intended for handling broken or truncated streams.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Jbig2Ctx.
Caller should check the returned int for status; exact return codes/semantics are unknown from this header.

functions.name: jbig2_ctx_new
functions.signature: Jbig2Ctx *jbig2_ctx_new(Jbig2Allocator *allocator, Jbig2Options options, Jbig2GlobalCtx *global_ctx, Jbig2ErrorCallback error_callback, void *error_callback_data);
functions.description: Creates and returns a new JBIG2 decoder context. This is the primary entry point for initializing the decoder before submitting data and retrieving decoded pages. In this header it is a function-like macro that forwards to jbig2_ctx_new_imp while automatically supplying the library’s major/minor version. Typical usage: create a context with jbig2_ctx_new, feed data via jbig2_data_in, obtain pages with jbig2_page_out, and finally free the context with jbig2_ctx_free. If allocator is NULL, a default malloc-based allocator is used. If error_callback is NULL, a default handler is used that prints fatal errors to stderr. Pass a non-NULL global_ctx (created with jbig2_make_global_ctx) when decoding embedded streams; otherwise pass NULL. Other behavioral details (e.g., failure modes) are not documented here and may need to be confirmed in the implementation or external docs.
requirements: allocator may be NULL to use the default malloc-based allocator (explicitly documented).
If allocator is non-NULL, its function pointers (alloc, free, realloc) must be valid and callable for the lifetime of the returned Jbig2Ctx (inferred from allocator usage).

options should be a valid combination of Jbig2Options flags; JBIG2_OPTIONS_EMBEDDED indicates embedded-stream mode (explicit from enum name/comment; specific allowed combinations beyond this are unknown).

global_ctx may be NULL for normal decoding; for embedded streams it should be a valid Jbig2GlobalCtx obtained via jbig2_make_global_ctx and kept alive while in use (inferred from "global context for embedded streams").
error_callback may be NULL to select the default handler that prints fatal errors to stderr (explicitly documented).

If error_callback is non-NULL, it must match Jbig2ErrorCallback signature and may be called by the library with severity and segment index information; error_callback_data is an opaque pointer provided back on callbacks and must remain valid for the lifetime of the context (inferred from callback pattern).
The macro injects version numbers; callers must not attempt to pass version values—use jbig2_ctx_new as declared here (explicit from macro definition).

Return-on-failure behavior is not specified in this header; callers should defensively check for a NULL return to detect initialization/allocation failure (unknown in docs; recommended based on standard C API patterns).

jbig2_global_ctx_free

unharnessable_functions.name: jbig2_ctx_new_imp
unharnessable_functions.reason: This internal entry requires correct library version numbers supplied by the jbig2_ctx_new macro, which the harness cannot reliably determine or validate.

data_types.description: Arbitrary raw bytes representing a JBIG2-encoded data stream or segment data. This is binary data consumed by a JBIG2 decoder via jbig2_data_in; it may include headers, segments, symbol dictionaries, text regions, patterns, and other JBIG2 structures. Any sequence of bytes is accepted; valid JBIG2 content follows the JBIG2 specification, but fuzzing may provide malformed or truncated data.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# JBIG2 byte generator
# Goal: produce valid/near-valid JBIG2 streams that exercise different code paths,
# including: full file header + segments, standalone segments, page info, symbol dict,
# text region, end-of-page/end-of-file markers, and mixed big/little details.
# Keep under 4096 bytes.

MAGIC = b"\x97JB2\x0D\x1A\x1A\x00"  # Standard JBIG2 file signature

# Utilities

def _rand_bits(r: random.Random, nbits: int) -> int:
    return r.getrandbits(nbits)

def _rand_u32(r: random.Random) -> int:
    return r.randrange(0, 2**32)

def _rand_u16(r: random.Random) -> int:
    return r.randrange(0, 2**16)

def _u32be(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _u16be(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)

def _u8(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack("B", x & 0xFF)

# JBIG2 segment helpers
# Segment header (per ISO/IEC 14492):
#  - segment number: 4 bytes (BE)
#  - segment header flags: 1 byte
#     bit7-5: segment type (0..63); type 48 indicates end of page, 51 end of file
#     bit4: page association size (0: 1 byte, 1: 4 bytes)
#     bit3-0: referred-to segment count (if 7 then long form follows)
#  - referred-to segment data (variable)
#  - page association (1 or 4 bytes)
#  - segment data length: 4 bytes (BE); may be 0xFFFFFFFF for unknown
#  - referred-to segment numbers (variable, BE each)

# For simplicity we will use short referred-to count (<=4) and short page association (1 byte)
# unless specifically testing the long/4-byte form.

SEG_TYPE_SYMBOL_DICT = 0
SEG_TYPE_TEXT_REGION = 4
SEG_TYPE_PATTERN_DICT = 16
SEG_TYPE_TABLES = 53  # not used but reserved
SEG_TYPE_END_OF_PAGE = 48
SEG_TYPE_END_OF_STRIPE = 49
SEG_TYPE_END_OF_FILE = 51
SEG_TYPE_PAGE_INFO = 50


def _segment_header(seg_num: int, seg_type: int, page_assoc_4: bool, ref_ids: List[int], page: int, length: int) -> bytes:
    # flags
    referred_count = len(ref_ids)
    long_ref_count = 7 if referred_count > 4 else referred_count
    flags = ((seg_type & 0x3F) << 5) & 0xE0  # actually seg_type is 0..63 mapped to bits7..2 in spec; but many decoders use 5 bits. We'll place in top bits.
    # Correct placement per spec: bits 7..2 are type; bits1 is page assoc size; bits0.. are referred count short
    # We'll form: type(6 bits) in high; page_assoc bit; low 3-4 bits ref count
    flags = (seg_type & 0x3F) << 2
    if page_assoc_4:
        flags |= 0x02
    flags |= (long_ref_count & 0x07)

    out = bytearray()
    out += _u32be(seg_num)
    out += _u8(flags)

    # referred-to segment data; for short count (<=4), a single byte of retention flags may appear; keep simplest: 0 (all new)
    if referred_count <= 4:
        # one byte of referred-to segment retention flags
        out += _u8(0)
    else:
        # Long form: not commonly needed; skip for now
        pass

    # page association
    if page_assoc_4:
        out += _u32be(page)
    else:
        out += _u8(page & 0xFF)

    # segment data length
    out += _u32be(length)

    # referred-to segment numbers (BE)
    for rid in ref_ids:
        out += _u32be(rid)

    return bytes(out)


def _page_info_segment(seg_num: int, r: random.Random, page: int) -> bytes:
    # Page info segment data is 11 bytes in spec
    # Fields (big-endian where multibyte):
    #  - width (4), height (4), xres (1), yres (1), flags (1)
    width = r.randrange(16, 2048)
    height = r.randrange(16, 2048)
    xres = r.choice([0, 72, 150, 200, 300, 400]) & 0xFF
    yres = r.choice([0, 72, 150, 200, 300, 400]) & 0xFF
    # flags: bits include default pixel, combination operator, etc. We'll pick common defaults.
    flags = r.randrange(0, 256)
    data = _u32be(width) + _u32be(height) + _u8(xres) + _u8(yres) + _u8(flags)
    hdr = _segment_header(seg_num, SEG_TYPE_PAGE_INFO, False, [], page, len(data))
    return hdr + data


def _symbol_dict_segment(seg_num: int, r: random.Random, page: int, num_syms: int) -> bytes:
    # Minimalistic symbol dictionary segment: header fields then arithmetic-coded data (we'll keep empty or trivial)
    # For decoder robustness, provide plausible header then zero-length payload (decoder should accept with checks)
    # SD header (per spec): 18 bytes minimal before data; but decoders often accept zero symbols
    # We'll encode numExportedSyms= num_syms, numNewSyms=num_syms, flags random
    flags = r.randrange(0, 1 << 16)
    num_export = num_syms
    num_new = num_syms
    # Huff/arith flags etc simplified
    header = _u16be(flags) + _u32be(num_export) + _u32be(num_new)
    # Add some bytes as coded table placeholders
    payload = header + bytes(r.randrange(0, 8))
    hdr = _segment_header(seg_num, SEG_TYPE_SYMBOL_DICT, False, [], page, len(payload))
    return hdr + payload


def _text_region_segment(seg_num: int, r: random.Random, page: int, ref_dict: int | None) -> bytes:
    # Text region referencing symbol dictionary optionally
    # Data: region segment info (rectangle, flags) + minimal strips
    x = r.randrange(0, 64)
    y = r.randrange(0, 64)
    w = r.randrange(8, 512)
    h = r.randrange(8, 256)
    flags = r.randrange(0, 256)
    region = _u32be(x) + _u32be(y) + _u32be(w) + _u32be(h) + _u8(flags)
    # Minimal text data stub
    text_payload = region + bytes(r.randrange(0, 16))
    refs = [ref_dict] if ref_dict is not None else []
    hdr = _segment_header(seg_num, SEG_TYPE_TEXT_REGION, False, refs, page, len(text_payload))
    return hdr + text_payload


def _end_of_page(seg_num: int, page: int) -> bytes:
    hdr = _segment_header(seg_num, SEG_TYPE_END_OF_PAGE, False, [], page, 0)
    return hdr


def _end_of_file(seg_num: int) -> bytes:
    hdr = _segment_header(seg_num, SEG_TYPE_END_OF_FILE, False, [], 0xFF, 0)
    return hdr


def _build_full_file(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    out += MAGIC
    # File header flags: 1 byte - 0x00 no pages unknown? Next 4 or 8 bytes depending flags; keep simple.
    # We'll use file header with unknown number of pages and no global segments (flag bit 0 = 0 -> #pages unknown? implement common: 0x00 means unknown pages, then no 4-byte field; but many decoders expect a 4-byte 0 for unknown pages when flag bit 0 set). To remain broadly compatible, set bit0=1 and write page count.
    flags = 0x01
    out += _u8(flags)
    num_pages = r.randrange(1, 3)
    out += _u32be(num_pages)

    seg_num = 1
    page = 1

    # Optional global segments probability
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        # Create a global symbol dict and an end-of-file in global stream is not used here, but we can mark as page 0xFFFF
        out += _symbol_dict_segment(seg_num, r, 0xFF, r.randrange(0, 4))
        seg_num += 1

    # Page loop
    for p in range(1, num_pages + 1):
        out += _page_info_segment(seg_num, r, p)
        seg_num += 1
        have_dict = r.random() < 0.9
        dict_id = None
        if have_dict:
            out += _symbol_dict_segment(seg_num, r, p, r.randrange(0, 6))
            dict_id = seg_num
            seg_num += 1
        # one or two text regions
        for _ in range(r.randrange(1, 3)):
            out += _text_region_segment(seg_num, r, p, dict_id if r.random() < 0.8 else None)
            seg_num += 1
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            out += _end_of_page(seg_num, p)
            seg_num += 1

    if r.random() < 0.7:
        out += _end_of_file(seg_num)

    return bytes(out)


def _build_segment_stream(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a stream without file header (embedded or chunked feed)
    out = bytearray()
    seg_num = 1
    page = r.randrange(1, 5)
    # A mix of segments
    out += _page_info_segment(seg_num, r, page); seg_num += 1
    sd_first = r.random() < 0.7
    dict_id = None
    if sd_first:
        out += _symbol_dict_segment(seg_num, r, page, r.randrange(1, 8))
        dict_id = seg_num
        seg_num += 1
    # text region referencing dict (or not)
    out += _text_region_segment(seg_num, r, page, dict_id if r.random() < 0.8 else None); seg_num += 1
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        out += _end_of_page(seg_num, page); seg_num += 1
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        out += _end_of_file(seg_num)
    return bytes(out)


def _build_minimal_header_only(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Just a header with 0 pages but valid structure
    out = bytearray()
    out += MAGIC
    flags = 0x01
    out += _u8(flags)
    out += _u32be(0)
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        out += _end_of_file(1)
    return bytes(out)


def _choose_builder(r: random.Random):
    return r.choices(
        population=[_build_full_file, _build_segment_stream, _build_minimal_header_only],
        weights=[0.6, 0.35, 0.05],
        k=1,
    )[0]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    builder = _choose_builder(r)
    data = builder(r)
    # Ensure size constraint
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]
    return data
